chunks: ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Ḍurays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who set out as a pilgrim for the Hajj of Islam, then died on the way.
He عليه السلام said: “If he died in the ḥaram, then the Hajj of Islam has sufficed for him. But if he died short of the ḥaram, then his heir should perform the Hajj of Islam on his behalf.”

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْ: it sufficed and discharged the obligation
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred precinct whose entry affects the legal ruling here
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required in Islam
key_terms.فَلْيَقْضِ: let him fulfill or make up the obligation on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his heir or guardian responsible for acting on his behalf

ai.seo_question: If someone dies on the way to hajj, does their obligatory Hajj of Islam count as fulfilled?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person who begins the obligatory hajj but dies before completing it. If death occurs within the sacred precinct, the obligation is considered fulfilled; if it occurs before reaching it, the heir must arrange the Hajj of Islam on his behalf.
